Figure 1:Replacing the resource-intensive teacher–critic stack with
direct representation distribution matching for few-step causal video
post-training.DMD-based post-training requires three video diffusion networks: a heavy frozen
score teacher, an online critic, and the generator itself.
ViRDM instead
matches generated videos directly against a fixed offline representation
distribution and updates only the generator. In the same 8-A100
parallelized training setting, this reduces peak memory from 77.1 to 48.3 GB per GPU and
post-training time from 22 to 2 hours, while improving the VBench Total from 84.51 to 84.87.

Figure 3:Qualitative comparison of different initialization.We show frames 0, 40, and 80 from two generated videos, separated by the
vertical dashed line, after the same causal few-step video RDM post-training. Each row uses a
different initialization. “Bid” denotes the original bidirectional model
without causal adaptation, “TF” teacher forcing, “CD” consistency
distillation, and “ODE” probability-flow ODE distillation. TF is a causal
multi-step initialization, whereas CD and ODE are causal few-step
initializations. Directly starting from the bidirectional model
causes severe drift under chunkwise causal generation. Teacher forcing
prevents this failure and preserves the scene, but produces substantially
weaker dynamics; the few-step causal initializations maintain coherence while
supporting stronger temporal evolution. This comparison visually supports
the quantitative results inTable3: causal compatibility
is essential for stable causal few-step video RDM, while few-step specialization helps
its final dynamics operating point.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison of different representation choices and dynamics
regularization.We show frames 0, 40, and 80 from two generated
videos, separated by the vertical dashed line. “Image Marginals” uses
independently encoded DINOv2 frame representations, whereas “Video
Marginal” uses a V-JEPA 2.1 contextual representation of the complete
video. The final row further adds the flow-based dynamics regularizer. Image marginals
produce little temporal evolution; the video marginal provides a stronger
dynamics signal, and explicit dynamics regularization further increases
sustained temporal change while preserving the scene and subject.

Figure 7:Qualitative results for the four-step bidirectional
extension.We show six generated videos, with frames 0, 40, and 80 from each
video displayed from left to right. The same ViRDM training recipe used for our
causal model also produces high-quality videos with clear temporal evolution
when applied to a bidirectional Wan2.1-1.3B generator.
